newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid rises amid higher natgas prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid rises amid higher natgas prices.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices rose Monday against Friday's assessments amid higher natural gas prices, brokers and traders said.
"Prices firmed a little," one Houston trader said.
The ongoing climb in natgas values remained a supportive factor for firmness in both the cash and paper resid prices, they said.

In the New York harbor, one percent sulfur resid grade was quoted at $17.50-$17.75 a barrel, compared with Friday's range of $17.00-$17.25. The three-percent grade was valued at $15.00-$15.25, up from $14.75-$15.25 on Thursday.

In the paper market, one-percent NYH prices were quoted at $17.50-$17.85, up from Friday's range of $17.30-$17.50, and three-percent in the Gulf Coast was pegged at $15.80-$16.20, also up from $15.60-$15.85.
In the Gulf physical market, prices for the one-percent grade ended at $16.00-$16.25, flat from Friday's range. Three-percent values were quoted at $15.75-$16.00, higher than $15.25-$15.75 on Friday.
New York city gate September gas prices were assessed at $2.07 today, versus NYH one percent resid at a $2.84/mmBtu equivalent. On Friday, September New York city gate gas was pegged at $2.05.
